description: Design a 4-to-1 multiplexer in Verilog. The multiplexer should take four input signals (I0, I1, I2, I3) and two select lines (S0, S1) and output one of the inputs based on the select lines. The output should be valid for all combinations of the select lines.
code:
module mux4to1 (
    input wire [3:0] I,  // 4-bit input
    input wire [1:0] S,  // 2-bit select
    output wire Y        // output
);
    assign Y = (S == 2'b00) ? I[0] :
               (S == 2'b01) ? I[1] :
               (S == 2'b10) ? I[2] :
               (S == 2'b11) ? I[3] : 1'b0; // Default case (though should never happen)
endmodule

description: Design a clock divider that divides the input clock frequency by a factor of 4. The output clock signal should toggle every 4 input clock cycles. The input is a clock signal, and the output is the divided clock signal.

Design a 16-bit deserializer that takes in an 8-bit input data stream and a clock signal. The deserializer should output the 16-bit data after two clock cycles. The first 8 bits should be output in the first clock cycle and the second 8 bits should be output in the second clock cycle. It should also have a reset signal that initializes the output to zero when asserted.
code:
module deserializer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg [15:0] data_out
);
    reg [1:0] state;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            data_out <= 16'b0;
            state <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin
                    data_out[7:0] <= data_in; // First 8 bits
                    state <= 2'b01;
                end
                2'b01: begin
                    data_out[15:8] <= data_in; // Second 8 bits
                    state <= 2'b00; // Go back to initial state
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a positive edge-triggered D-flip-flop with asynchronous reset. The D-flip-flop should have inputs for data (D), clock (CLK), and reset (RST). On the rising edge of the clock, if reset is not asserted, the output (Q) should take the value of D. If reset is asserted, the output Q should be set to 0.

Design a DVFS controller that adjusts the voltage and frequency of a system based on a given temperature input. The controller should have the following features:
1. It has an input temperature (in degrees Celsius) that ranges from 0 to 100.
2. Based on the temperature input, the controller should output a voltage and frequency setting according to the following criteria:
   - Temperature < 40: Voltage = 1.0V, Frequency = 1.0GHz
   - 40 ≤ Temperature < 70: Voltage = 1.2V, Frequency = 1.5GHz
   - Temperature ≥ 70: Voltage = 1.5V, Frequency = 2.0GHz
3. The state should retain the last value until a new temperature value is provided.
code:
module dvfs_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [6:0] temperature, // 0 to 100
    output reg [3:0] voltage, // 1.0V = 4'b0001, 1.2V = 4'b0010, 1.5V = 4'b0011
    output reg [3:0] frequency // 1.0GHz = 4'b0001, 1.5GHz = 4'b0010, 2.0GHz = 4'b0011
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            voltage <= 4'b0001; // Default to 1.0V
            frequency <= 4'b0001; // Default to 1.0GHz
        end else begin
            if (temperature < 40) begin
                voltage <= 4'b0001; // 1.0V
                frequency <= 4'b0001; // 1.0GHz
            end else if (temperature < 70) begin
                voltage <= 4'b0010; // 1.2V
                frequency <= 4'b0010; // 1.5GHz
            end else begin
                voltage <= 4'b0011; // 1.5V
                frequency <= 4'b0011; // 2.0GHz
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 3-tap Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter. The filter will take in 3 input samples and produce a single output sample, where the output is calculated as the sum of the weighted input samples. Use weights of 1, 2, and 1 for the first, second, and third samples respectively.

Design a 4-to-2 priority encoder. The encoder should output a 2-bit binary representation of the highest priority active input. The priority of the inputs is such that input 3 has the highest priority, followed by input 2, input 1, and input 0 has the lowest priority. If no inputs are active, the output should be '00'. Design a simple Model Predictive Control (MPC) module that takes a 4-bit input for the current state and a 4-bit input for the desired state. The module will output a control signal that adjusts the current state towards the desired state in a step-wise manner. The control signal should be a 4-bit output that indicates the adjustment needed. The control logic should update the current state on the rising edge of a clock signal.
code:
module mpc_controller (
    input clk,
    input [3:0] current_state,
    input [3:0] desired_state,
    output reg [3:0] control_signal
);
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (current_state < desired_state) begin
            control_signal <= current_state + 1; // Increment towards desired state
        end else if (current_state > desired_state) begin
            control_signal <= current_state - 1; // Decrement towards desired state
        end else begin
            control_signal <= current_state; // No change if states are equal
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a fixed-priority arbiter with three request lines (req[2:0]) and one grant line (grant). The arbiter should grant access to the highest priority request. The priority is: req[2] > req[1] > req[0]. If multiple requests are made at the same time, the arbiter should grant permission to the highest priority request first. The state should be retained until a grant is made and the request is deasserted.
code:
module fixed_priority_arbiter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire [2:0] req,
    output reg [2:0] grant
);
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            grant <= 3'b000;
        end else begin
            grant <= 3'b000; // Default no grant
            if (req[2]) begin
                grant <= 3'b100; // Grant req[2]
            end else if (req[1]) begin
                grant <= 3'b010; // Grant req[1]
            end else if (req[0]) begin
                grant <= 3'b001; // Grant req[0]
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Design an I2C master controller that generates the start condition, stop condition, and sends an address to the slave device. The master should also acknowledge the receipt of the address from the slave. Design a simple cache memory system with a FIFO cache replacement policy. The cache will have a fixed size of 4 blocks. Implement the following features: 
1. A way to write data to the cache (if the cache is full, evict the oldest block).
2. A way to read data from the cache.
3. A status signal that indicates if the requested data was found in the cache (hit) or not (miss).
code:
module CacheFIFO (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] address, // 8-bit address
    input wire [7:0] data_in, // data to write
    input wire write_enable,    // write signal
    output reg [7:0] data_out,  // data output
    output reg hit              // hit signal
);
    reg [7:0] cache [0:3];      // cache storage (4 blocks)
    reg [1:0] lru [0:3];         // LRU tracking
    integer i, oldest;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            // Initialize cache and hit signal
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                cache[i] <= 8'b0;
                lru[i] <= 2'b0;
            end
            hit <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            hit <= 1'b0; // Reset hit signal for this cycle
            
            // Check for Cache Hit
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                if (cache[i] == address) begin
                    hit <= 1'b1;
                    data_out <= cache[i]; // Return data from cache
                end
            end
            
            // Cache Write Operation
            if (write_enable) begin
                // Find the oldest block to replace
                oldest = 0;
                for (i = 1; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (lru[i] > lru[oldest]) begin
                        oldest = i;
                    end
                end

                // Replace the oldest block
                cache[oldest] <= address; // Store new data in the cache
                lru[oldest] <= 2'b0; // Reset LRU for the new block
                // Update LRU counters
                for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (i != oldest) begin
                        lru[i] <= lru[i] + 1; // Increment LRU for other blocks
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 2-channel DMA controller that can transfer data from a memory source to a memory destination. The controller should manage two channels, each capable of transferring a specified number of bytes upon receiving a start signal. Design a Master-Slave D-Latch in Verilog. The D-Latch should have inputs for Data (D), a Clock (CLK), and an active-high enable (EN) signal. The output should reflect the input D when CLK is high and EN is also high, and hold the last value when CLK goes low or EN is low.

Design a divide-by-2 circuit using a flip-flop. The input will be a clock signal and a reset signal, and the output will be the divided clock signal. The circuit should reset on the reset signal and toggle the output on each rising edge of the clock.

Design a simple memory allocator in Verilog that allows allocation and deallocation of a fixed-size memory block using a simple linked list. The allocator should support a maximum of 5 blocks of memory. Each block can be allocated or freed based on a request signal. The memory allocation signal should raise an output flag when a memory block is successfully allocated. The deallocation should clear the block's status.
code:
module memory_allocator(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [2:0] req_size, // Request for block size (1-5)
    input alloc,          // Request to allocate memory
    input free,          // Request to free memory
    output reg [4:0] memory_status, // Memory status (1: allocated, 0: free)
    output reg alloc_success // Allocation success flag
);
    reg [4:0] mem_block; // Memory blocks representation (5 blocks)
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            mem_block <= 5'b00000;
            alloc_success <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (alloc) begin
                if (mem_block[req_size-1] == 0) begin // Check if the block is free
                    mem_block[req_size-1] <= 1; // Allocate memory
                    alloc_success <= 1; // Set success flag
                end else begin
                    alloc_success <= 0; // Already allocated
                end
            end else if (free) begin
                mem_block[req_size-1] <= 0; // Free memory
                alloc_success <= 0; // Clear success flag
            end
            memory_status <= mem_block; // Update output memory status
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a SRT (Sweeney, Robertson, and Tocher) divider in Verilog that takes a 16-bit input dividend and a 16-bit input divisor. The quotient should be a 16-bit output, and the remainder should be a 16-bit output. Create a noise suppression circuit that takes a 5-bit input signal and outputs a cleaned 5-bit signal. The circuit should suppress any signal that has a noise value greater than 2 bits different from the majority value of the input signal.

Design an 8-bit SRAM cell that can store a single byte of data. The SRAM cell should have an input data bus (data_in), a read enable (read_en), a write enable (write_en), an address input (addr), and an output data bus (data_out). When write_en is high, the data on data_in should be stored in the memory at the specified address. When read_en is high, the stored data at the specified address should be output on data_out.
code:
module sram_8bit (  
    input wire [7:0] data_in,  
    input wire read_en,  
    input wire write_en,  
    input wire [2:0] addr,  
    output reg [7:0] data_out  
);  
    reg [7:0] memory [0:7]; // 8x8 SRAM memory  

    always @(posedge write_en or posedge read_en) begin  
        if (write_en) begin  
            memory[addr] <= data_in; // Write data to memory  
        end  
        if (read_en) begin  
            data_out <= memory[addr]; // Read data from memory  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

Design a temperature-based shutdown controller that monitors the temperature of a system. If the temperature exceeds a threshold (let's say 75 degrees), the system should initiate a shutdown sequence. The shutdown process takes 5 clock cycles. code:

);

description: Design an 8-channel DMA (Direct Memory Access) controller that allows multiple data transfers from memory to peripheral devices. The controller should have a control signal input that indicates when a transfer should occur, a select input to choose one of the 8 channels, and a data input for the data to be transferred. The output should indicate the status of the transfer for each channel (active or inactive). The DMA controller should also include a ready signal that indicates when the controller is ready for the next transfer.
code:
module dma_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start_transfer,
    input wire [2:0] channel_select,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg [7:0] status_out,
    output reg ready
);
    
    reg [7:0] channel_status;
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            channel_status <= 8'b00000000;
            status_out <= 8'b00000000;
            ready <= 1'b1;
        end else begin
            if (start_transfer && ready) begin
                channel_status[channel_select] <= 1'b1; // Set the selected channel active
                status_out <= channel_status; // Output the current status
                ready <= 1'b0; // Not ready for next transfer until done
            end
            if (~start_transfer) begin
                channel_status[channel_select] <= 1'b0; // Reset the selected channel
                ready <= 1'b1; // Ready for next transfer
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

It should have inputs for push data, a push signal, a pop signal, and an output for the popped data. Additionally, it should have an output indicating if the stack is empty.

Create a 4-to-1 multiplexer with enable. The multiplexer should select one of the four input data lines based on the 2-bit select line. An enable signal should control whether the output is valid (if enable is high) or always zero (if enable is low).

Design a 4-element merge sort module in Verilog that sorts a 4-bit input array. The module should take a 16-bit input representing four 4-bit integers and output a 16-bit sorted output. The sorting should be performed using the merge sort algorithm.

Design a 2nd order Chebyshev low-pass filter using combinational logic. The filter should accept a 5-bit binary input representing the signal and produce a 5-bit binary output representing the filtered signal.

Design a simple 8-bit DRAM cell with read and write capabilities. The DRAM cell should have inputs for data (8 bits), a write enable signal (we), a read enable signal (re), and an output for the data read (out). The cell should be able to store data when the write enable signal is high and should output the stored data when the read enable signal is high.
code:
module dram_cell (

    input wire we,
    input wire re,
    output reg [7:0] out
);
    reg [7:0] memory;

    always @(posedge we or posedge re) begin
        if (we) begin
            memory <= data; // Write data to memory
        end
        if (re) begin
            out <= memory; // Read data from memory
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 3x3 median filter in Verilog that takes a 3x3 matrix as input and outputs the median value. The matrix values will be provided as a flat array of 9 bits, representing pixel intensities.

Design a Huffman coding combinational circuit that takes a set of 8-bit binary values representing characters and outputs their corresponding Huffman encoded binary values. Assume the following character frequencies for the encoding:
- 'A': 5
- 'B': 9
- 'C': 12
- 'D': 13

The circuit should output the encoded values based on the above frequencies.
code:

    output reg [7:0] out_code
);
    always @(*) begin
        case (in_char)

Implement the Floyd-Warshall algorithm in Verilog to find the shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in a directed graph. The graph will be represented as an adjacency matrix with weights that can include infinity (represented as a large number) for no connection.
A 4-bit Parallel-in Serial-out (PISO) shift register that can load data in parallel, shift out the data serially, and control the shifting with a clock and a load signal.

Design a 16-bit wide 2-to-1 multiplexer. The multiplexer should select between two 16-bit inputs (A and B) based on a 1-bit select signal (sel). The output (Y) should be the selected input based on the value of sel.
A simple 8-bit timer circuit that counts up every clock cycle. It should have a reset input to set the timer to zero and a maximum value of 255, at which it rolls over to 0.

Design a LIFO (Last In First Out) stack in Verilog. The stack should support push and pop operations. The stack has a fixed depth (e.g., 4). It should also have an output to indicate whether the stack is empty or full.

Design a  SR flip-flop in Verilog. The SR flip-flop should have two inputs (S and R) and one output (Q). The flip-flop should set Q to 1 when S is high and reset Q to 0 when R is high, with the condition that both S and R should not be high simultaneously.

Design a simple EEPROM cell that can perform the following operations:
1. Write a single bit of data (0 or 1).
2. Read the stored bit.
3. Provide a reset function to clear the stored bit to 0.
The EEPROM should have inputs for data to write, a write enable signal, a reset signal, and an output for the stored data.
code:

    input wire write_enable,

);

description: Design a 32-bit up counter that increments its value on each rising edge of the clock. The counter should reset to zero when the reset signal is asserted. Provide a way to load a specific value into the counter through a load input signal. If load is high, the counter should load the input value instead of incrementing.

A Watchdog Timer that resets a system if no input signal is received within a specified timeout period. The timer counts clock cycles when a reset signal is not asserted, and if it reaches the maximum count, it generates a reset output.
code:
module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n, // active low reset
    input wire feed,  // input signal to reset the timer
    output reg reset_out // output reset signal
);
    parameter TIMEOUT = 5'd10; // timeout period
    reg [4:0] count; // 5-bit counter

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            count <= 5'd0;
            reset_out <= 1'b0;
        end else if (feed) begin
            count <= 5'd0; // reset count if fed
            reset_out <= 1'b0; // clear reset output
        end else if (count < TIMEOUT) begin
            count <= count + 1;
            reset_out <= 1'b0; // keep reset low while counting
        end else begin
            reset_out <= 1'b1; // assert reset if timeout reached
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a fan speed control system that adjusts the speed of a fan based on temperature readings. The system should have three speed settings: low, medium, and high. The fan's speed should increase with temperature. The temperature is represented as a 4-bit binary number (0000 to 1111), where 0000 corresponds to 0 degrees, and 1111 corresponds to 15 degrees. The speed settings are as follows: 
- 0-4 degrees: Low speed (00)
- 5-9 degrees: Medium speed (01)
- 10-15 degrees: High speed (10)
The fan speed should be stored in a 2-bit register.
code:
module fan_speed_control(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [3:0] temperature,
    output reg [1:0] fan_speed
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            fan_speed <= 2'b00; // Default to low speed
        end else begin
            case (temperature)
                4'b0000, 4'b0001, 4'b0010, 4'b0011, 4'b0100: fan_speed <= 2'b00; // Low speed
                4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1000, 4'b1001: fan_speed <= 2'b01; // Medium speed
                4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, 4'b1111: fan_speed <= 2'b10; // High speed
                default: fan_speed <= 2'b00; // Default to low speed
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

- req: 4-bit request signal from the peripherals
- ack: 4-bit acknowledgment signal to the peripherals

The controller should have the following outputs:

A 32-bit Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) that generates pseudo-random sequences. The register should shift its value on each clock cycle and apply a feedback mechanism using taps at certain bits determined by a polynomial. It must also reset to a user-defined seed value.
code:
module LFSR_32bit(  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input [31:0] seed,  
    output reg [31:0] lfsr_out  
);  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            lfsr_out <= seed;  
        end else begin  
            lfsr_out <= {lfsr_out[30:0], lfsr_out[31] ^ lfsr_out[21] ^ lfsr_out[1] ^ lfsr_out[0]};  
        end  
    end

description: Design a Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) in Verilog that takes an input clock signal and generates an output clock signal that is phase-aligned with the input. The PLL should have a frequency divider and a phase detector. The phase detected should control the frequency division ratio, thereby adjusting the output clock based on the input clock. The output clock should toggle at a certain frequency based on the divider settings.
code:
module PLL (
    input wire clk_in,          // Input clock
    input wire reset,           // Reset signal
    output reg clk_out          // Output clock
);

    reg [3:0] divider;          // Divider for output clock
    reg [3:0] counter;          // Counter for divider

    always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 0;
            clk_out <= 0;
            divider <= 4;      // Initial divider value
        end else begin
            if (counter >= divider) begin
                clk_out <= ~clk_out; // Toggle output clock
                counter <= 0;         // Reset counter
            end else begin
                counter <= counter + 1; // Increment counter
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Implement a Watchdog Timer in Verilog that resets a signal if it does not receive an input within a specified time period. The timer should start counting when the input signal is high, and if the timer expires (after a predefined limit), it should output a reset signal. The timer can be reset by receiving a new high input signal before it expires. Use a clock signal for the timing mechanism.

Design a GPIO controller that allows for reading and writing to a set of general-purpose input/output pins. The controller should have the following features:
1. A 4-bit input for data to be written to the GPIO pins.

description: Design a Verilog module that performs bilinear interpolation on a 2x2 grid of pixel values. );

Design a Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator (CSPRNG) using a Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) in Verilog. module CSPRNG (

    input wire reset,
    input wire [15:0] seed,
    output reg [15:0] random_out
);

            lfsr <= seed; // Load seed on reset

            window_status <= 0;
            ack <= 0;

                received_count <= received_count + 1;

    end

    input wire clk,
    input wire cs,
    input wire mosi,
    output reg miso,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg data_ready
);
    reg [2:0] bit_count;

        if (!cs) begin
            bit_count <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            data_ready <= 0;
        end else if (bit_count < 8) begin

            bit_count <= bit_count + 1;

            miso <= data_out[7]; // Send the MSB out
        end
    end

        if (data_ready) begin
            miso <= data_out[7]; // Continue sending data if ready
            data_out <= {data_out[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift out the next bit
            if (bit_count > 0) begin

            end else begin

        end
    end
endmodule
